note: Official weights. Changing the weights or how factors are computed MUST bump `version`; historical records keep the version that produced them and are not re-scored. 1.1 (2026-09): Growth is revenue growth alone; dGPOA moved to Quality. 1.2 (2026-09): below the ROIC hurdle growth is capped at 50 (min(p, 100-p)) instead of inverted, and figures come only from financial reports, never proxy statements. 1.3 (2026-09): Growth is the three-year trend of quarterly trailing revenue (annual CAGR as the fallback), and revenue is the largest of the nested revenue tags rather than the first by priority. 1.4 (2026-09): the change in gross profitability and earnings variability are current to the latest quarter (quarterly trailing windows, fiscal years as the fallback); debt comes from the most recent balance sheet that reports it; a company whose latest report is over 200 days old is not scored. 1.5 (2026-09): earnings variability is measured around the trend line where return on assets is rising, so steady improvement no longer reads as instability; a falling trend still counts in full. 1.6 (2026-09): Growth adds the latest year's change in operating income (four times the median quarterly year-on-year change, over average assets), and revenue growth is capped by the latest year when revenue fell. 1.7 (2026-09): that cap became an average - where revenue fell in the latest year, growth is the mean of the three-year trend and that year, so a collapse still scores near the bottom while a one-percent dip no longer erases a rising trend. 1.8 (2026-09): the convertible and senior notes that software filers tag alone are mapped, tags holding one slice of a borrowing stay unmapped on purpose, and a company whose entire filing history holds no borrowing at all is read as debt-free rather than unresolved. 1.9 (2026-09): one-off items a company tags itself - disposal gains, impairments, restructuring - are taken back out of EBIT in both directions together, so a write-down no longer reads as a broken business and a disposal no longer reads as profit. 1.10 (2026-09): earnings variability is measured on the same normalised basis - a tagged one-off is removed from the quarter or fiscal year it was booked in, after tax, so a write-down no longer reads as an unstable business. 2.0 (2026-09): four segments instead of three. Banks, insurers and asset managers are scored on return on equity and assets, earnings and book yields, equity/assets and the change in profit over assets, because enterprise-value metrics resolved for half of them and mean little for a business whose debt is its raw material; REITs get their own table scored on funds from operations (net income plus depreciation, one-off items removed), FFO yield, debt/assets and net debt/FFO, because depreciation on buildings that hold their value is not an economic cost. Growth is conditioned on return on equity for financials and on FFO over assets for REITs. 2.1 (2026-09): three corrections to how growth is scored. Revenue growth is the average of the three-year trend and the latest year in both directions, not only when the latest year fell, so a recovery counts as much as a collapse. Below the return hurdle a growth percentile is capped at the midpoint instead of mirrored, because min(p, 100-p) returned the same measurement with its sign flipped - a raw 98 came back as 2 - and jumped 96 points across a hurdle a tenth of a point can cross. And the change in operating income is no longer conditioned on the hurdle at all: it already measures the direction of profit, so inverting it meant the faster a company shrank its losses the worse it scored. The 2026-08 baseline was regenerated under each before any comparison depended on it - see the README correction log. 2.2 (2026-10): two corrections to the financials table. A bank's, an insurer's, a broker's and an asset manager's balance sheets differ by nature - a bank holds 6-9% equity against assets, an insurer 20% or more - so pooled in one cohort the equity and leverage metrics ranked every large bank in the bottom third (Bank of America 216th of 288) for being a bank; each is now ranked against its own kind. And JPMorgan, US Bancorp and others tag their whole long-term debt under a name that was not read, so only their short-term borrowings counted (JPMorgan's debt/equity read 0.19, not about 1.5); it is read now. The 2026-08 and 2026-09 records were regenerated under both - see the README correction log.
